fixes.explanation: Egypt is a long walk from this verse, baker. Paul isn't starting somewhere new at all. He says, “Let us go back and visit the brothers in every town where we proclaimed the word of the Lord…” (Acts 15:36). It's a return trip to visit the brothers in those towns, and Egypt isn't mentioned anywhere.

The text gives that reason, baker. It says Paul thought it best not to take Mark, John also called Mark, “…because he had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not accompanied them in the work.” That's the writer telling us why. I think it was a hard thing for both men to sit across from. (Acts 15:38)

That's the one, baker. “Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus…” Barnabas wanted to take Mark, and this verse shows him doing it. Paul went a different direction, since they parted company. (Acts 15:37, 39)
Crete is an island, so you were thinking in the right direction. But the text says Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus. Cyprus is the island in verse 39. (Acts 15:39)

Malta is an island too, friend, but it's not the one in this verse. The text says, “Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus…” Barnabas took Mark along and set sail. Cyprus is the place the verse names, and Malta never comes up. (Acts 15:39)

You got it, baker. Paul “…traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.” He's building people up, and Silas, the one Paul chose, is with him. That's a good way to spend a road trip. (Acts 15:40-41)

Warnings are in the Bible, but they're not what this verse says. Paul traveled through Syria and Cilicia, “…strengthening the churches.” The verse names strengthening, so that's the word that fits. (Acts 15:41)

That's right, baker. “Paul wanted Timothy to accompany him, so he took him…” Paul found a disciple the brothers spoke well of and brought him along. I think Timothy had a lot of road ahead of him. (Acts 16:2-3)

You got it, baker. Paul circumcised Timothy “…on account of the Jews in that area, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.” Timothy's mother was a believing Jewish woman, and the Jews in that area all knew his father was Greek. That is the reason the text gives. (Acts 16:1, 3)

You got it, baker. The text says, “During the night, Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia standing and pleading with him…” I think a plea like that gets your attention faster than a smoking oven. His words are “Come over to Macedonia and help us.” (Acts 16:9)
Galilee isn't in this vision, friend. Paul saw “…a man of Macedonia standing and pleading with him…” Macedonia is where the man is from, and it's where he's asking Paul to come. (Acts 16:9)

You got it, baker. As soon as Paul had seen the vision, they got ready to leave for Macedonia, “…concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.” They concluded it was God's call. The text says it plainly. (Acts 16:9-10)
Nobody in Troas is said to send them, baker. They got ready to leave “…concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.” The call they name is God's, not a church's. (Acts 16:10)
